verdict.rationale: Nitrokey's own OpenPGP-card documentation lists a 'Touch Confirmation (Nitrokey 3 only)' feature, and FIDO2 SSH keys are documented, so a physical touch can gate cryptographic operations such as signing and SSH authentication that an automated process would need. The evidence is only a section heading, though, with no detail on how touch is enforced or how it fits agent workflows. missing for 10: documented detail of touch-confirmation behavior and configuration, any guidance on using touch as an approval gate for automated or agent-initiated actions, independent or hands-on corroboration, support beyond Nitrokey 3.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can require a physical key touch as the human-approval step for sensitive automated or agent-initiated actions
